candidates.premise: Horsea can swim backward while continuing to face forward, using its rapidly moving dorsal fins.
candidates.hook: Horsea can flee without ever turning its back.

candidates.note: A distinctive, concrete movement mechanic directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries; the backward glide is immediately demonstrable.

candidates.premise: When ocean currents become dangerous, Horsea wraps its coiled tail around rocks or coral to stay anchored.
candidates.hook: Horsea's tail is secretly an anchor.
candidates.visualIdea: A current pushes Horsea across the screen until its tail coils around coral and holds it in place.
candidates.note: A clever survival adaptation with a clear before-and-after visual. Less unexpected than the ink sniper or backward swimming angles.

candidates.premise: Horsea swim with dance-like motions and compete to see which one can create the biggest whirlpool.
candidates.hook: Horsea turns swimming into a whirlpool competition.
candidates.visualIdea: Two Horsea perform synchronized fin movements while their whirlpools grow side by side.
candidates.note: The competition is genuinely surprising and highly visual, but the research does not provide a measurable contest rule or stakes beyond making the biggest whirlpool.
